new_concerns.text: Two conflicting versions of research.md are bundled with the plan. The second copy still specifies the simulated-null Type I error approach ('We have amended FR-004') and a GLMM with binomial link in Phase 5, contradicting the plan's T021 (label shuffling on real data, N=5000) and T024 (Friedman test) and the unamended spec FR-004/FR-008. Remove or align the stale research.md so the supporting design doc matches the plan and spec.

Two different research.md documents were submitted: one estimates Type I error "by shuffling group labels on the filtered real datasets" with a Friedman test (matching plan.md), the other uses "simulated null datasets" with a GLMM and N=2400 iterations. The docs contradict each other on the core methodology (FR-004) and the inference method (FR-008). Consolidate to a single research.md consistent with plan.md (real-data shuffling + Friedman).

responses.response: Removed the simulated-null amendment. Plan and research now estimate Type I error exactly as FR-004/US-2 mandate: by shuffling group labels on the filtered real datasets (multiple iterations, fixed seed). Simulated-null data is retained only as an optional diagnostic sanity check, never the primary estimate.
